title_candidates: GLM-5.2 makes long-context open models worth testing again
summary: Z.AI released GLM-5.2 with a 1M-token context claim, MIT licensing, and a focus on long-horizon coding and agent tasks.

primary_source.title: GLM-5.2: Built for Long-Horizon Tasks
primary_source.author: Z.AI
key_facts: Z.AI released GLM-5.2 as a flagship model for long-horizon tasks.
The post says GLM-5.2 supports a 1M-token context and is released under the MIT license.
Z.AI presents GLM-5.2 as aimed at sustained coding-agent work, complex debugging, automated research, and performance optimization.
The post describes effort-level control for balancing capability, speed, and cost.

prerequisites: A long document, code issue, or planning task you can safely test

steps.instruction: Open Z.ai chat or the GLM-5.2 Hugging Face page.
Choose a long but non-sensitive task, such as summarizing a public report or planning changes from a public issue.
Ask GLM-5.2 for an answer, then ask it to cite the exact parts of the input it relied on.
Run the same task in your usual model and compare missed details, invented details, and time spent.
Use GLM-5.2 only where long-context recall or open-model control clearly beats your current tool.
